question.text: 'Vindhya Credit' Cat II AIF has signed a side letter with one LP granting enhanced reporting rights. The chapter's guidance on side letters states:

answer.text: All side letters are prohibited under SEBI (AIF) Regulations
Side letters are permitted only for foreign institutional investors
Side letters must be approved by SEBI for every LP individually
The existence of a side letter should have objective justification, and MFN usage should be regularised so that investors are not afforded special/additional rights arbitrarily

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p.311, the existence of a side letter should have objective justification. Per p.301, MFN usage in side letters should be regularised so that investors are not afforded special or additional rights arbitrarily. Per p.528, differential rights via side letters or agreements are supported by current disclosure and pari-passu treatment requirements. The Trap: Side letters are not prohibited under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, SEBI does not approve each side letter individually, and there is no foreign-investor-only restriction in the source. Note: The framework permits side letters subject to objective justification, MFN regularisation, and disclosure/pari-passu treatment of differential rights.
